oracle.engine: dss_capi 0.15.0b4 (OpenDSS SVN r4103); regenerated for WP-U1.6 D12 (SwtControl Normal/State field mapping). WP-U2.4 D6: `swtcontrol_action_open` removed and `swtcontrol_makelike` re-based on `state=open` — EPRI r4133 makes the deprecated `Action` force the ACTUAL state (State=open), which capi015 (this golden's oracle) does NOT (State=closed), so it is no longer default-oracle-pinnable; the D6 behavior is pinned by the swt_control unit tests + the r4133 live decks (swtcontrol_time/midi). `state=open` forces the switch identically on capi015/0.14.5 and r4133, so makelike's State=open is oracle-derived (== swtcontrol_state_open). Values render lowercase (0.14.5/Rust enum), matching the port's `?` surface. The `swtcontrol_locked_then_action` scenario was dropped: capi015 raises the strict PermissiveProperties read-only error (#2024106) on a locked `Action=` write, which the port deliberately does NOT adopt (ledger L2 / C2 dss-ext-only surface) — it silently ignores, unit-pinned by `locked_ignores_action_write` / `locked_ignores_normal_and_state_writes`. R4133_PROPS RP3.7 (per-phase switch state): the 10 `Normal`/`State` cells below no longer carry capi015's scalar render. r4133 keeps per-phase state (`Version8/Source/Controls/SwtControl.pas:37-38`, `:453-480`) and its getters render one token per CONTROLLED-ELEMENT phase (`:589-599` Normal / `:600-610` State), a surface no capi-line engine has; the overlaid values are the official EPRI r4133 DLL's own bytes, measured by replaying these five scenarios through the epri-worker bridge with this gate's `clear` + `new circuit.propsprobe` preamble (tmp probe, RP3.7 A2b). `swtcontrol_default`/`swtcontrol_lock_delay` Normal moves off capi015's unset `''` because r4133's `Create` initializes BOTH arrays all-CLOSED (`:299-305`). Every other cell of these scenarios is untouched capi015 and still compares as before (the r4133 DLL diverges on SwitchedObj case, the `Action`/`Reset`/`Enabled` echoes and the `Delay` store-vs-live read - pre-existing pairs owned elsewhere, not overlaid here).
